feedback.problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2} & \frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{3}{2} & -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}t-3 \\ 2t+1\end{aligned}]
$$

The complementary solution to this system is given by

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Then, the general solution of the system is

| $x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+\,\,$ |  | $-\frac{7}{4}$ |  | $\,\,t+\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  | . |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term

$$
[\begin{aligned}t-3 \\ 2t+1\end{aligned}]
$$

of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is polynomial of degree $1.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also polynomial of degree $1,$ i.e.

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}t+{b}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

where ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{b}_{1},{b}_{2}$  are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the derivative of ${x}_{p}$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{x}_{p}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the unknown constants, we substitute ${x}_{p}$ and ${x}_{p}^{′}$ into our system:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1/2 & 3/2 \\ 3/2 & -1/2\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} \\ {b}_{2}\end{aligned}])+[\begin{aligned}t-3 \\ 2t+1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}({a}_{1}t+{b}_{1})+\frac{3}{2}({a}_{2}t+{b}_{2}) \\ \frac{3}{2}({a}_{1}t+{b}_{1})-\frac{1}{2}({a}_{2}t+{b}_{2})\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t-3 \\ 2t+1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0t+{a}_{1} \\ 0t+{a}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}(-\frac{{a}_{1}}{2}+\frac{3{a}_{2}}{2}+1)t+(-\frac{{b}_{1}}{2}+\frac{3{b}_{2}}{2}-3) \\ (\frac{3{a}_{1}}{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}}{2}+2)t+(\frac{3{b}_{1}}{2}-\frac{{b}_{2}}{2}+1)\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-\frac{{a}_{1}}{2}+\frac{3{a}_{2}}{2}+1=0 \\ \frac{3{a}_{1}}{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}}{2}+2=0 \\ -\frac{{b}_{1}}{2}+\frac{3{b}_{2}}{2}-3={a}_{1} \\ \frac{3{b}_{1}}{2}-\frac{{b}_{2}}{2}+1={a}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first two equations, we get 

$$
{a}_{1}=-\frac{7}{4},\,{a}_{2}=-\frac{5}{4}.
$$

 
Substituting these into the third and fourth equations, and solving for ${b}_{1}$ and ${b}_{2},$ we have

$$
{b}_{1}=-\frac{11}{8},\,{b}_{2}=\frac{3}{8}.
$$

 

Therefore, the particular solution is

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{7}{4} \\ -\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{11}{8} \\ \frac{3}{8}\end{aligned}].
$$
